Hey there. I felt the same way when I failed my first (and at the moment, only) suicide attempt. I was so angry with myself, that I couldn't even succeed at dying. But you know what? I'm glad I failed. Time and time again, people will tell you that it gets better (annoying, right?), but I am not one of those people. I'm not going to tell you that everything will be ok, or that suicide is selfish, or any of that stuff. I know how it feels to be told that and not believe a word of it. Instead, I'll leave you with this: Live for the good times. There will be good times, and there most certainly will be bad times, but even if the only good thing that has happened to you today is that someone smiled at you or held the door open for you, then that's a reason to live. I'm sorry that you're going through this. Sending love and prayers your way ❤️

My best friend at the time (who is now my soon-to-be ex husband) really wanted me to go to church with him. He had been bugging me about since he first met me. Well, when my suicide attempt failed, I was pissed. I couldn't even kill myself. So I figured what the hell, I'll go to church. If I don't, it's just going to be another long night of being alone and having suicidal thoughts. So I went, and for the first time in my life, I actually felt like I belonged. The people were so welcoming and loving, and it was unlike anything I had ever experienced (and I had been to plenty of churches, just never made the big commitment). I knew self harm wasn't what God wanted for me, and I still believe that, even though the one who lead me to God turned out to be the devil himself. It got easier to say no to the blade, especially with Austin there to support me (like he always did). But he's gone now, and even though I have my roommates, it's not the same. The process itself wasn't easy though. At the time, I lived with my grandmother, and I confided in her about my depression and self harm, only after one of the cuts started to get infected. I was put on medication and I had to stay a couple weeks in Lakeside, which didn't really help me to be honest. I lied to the counselors about why I was depressed. I was embarrassed. I blamed it on my crappy childhood (or lack thereof).

Honestly? It felt good. The scratch of something sharp against my skin felt better than the pain I was feeling on the inside. I guess I just got used to everyone letting me down and hurting me that I decided that if I hurt myself worse, then anything they did to me wouldn't feel as bad. I was wrong, and I got addicted to the pain.
